projects.name: Open source — Snapcraft and charmhub.io (Canonical)

projects.name: KRONOS — GREEDY ALGORITHM FOR SCHEDULING LECTURES BY SOFT CONSTRAINT OPTIMIZATION, KNUST
projects.about: An implementation of a greedy algorithm which schedules lectures into a workable weekly timetable, taking into consideration a weighted number of soft constraints including the comfort of lecturers and students and the distance between lecture halls. The project solves an NP-hard problem and replaced the manual method of scheduling, cutting timetable generation for the College of Engineering at Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology from 2 months to 10 minutes. It has been adopted by the College of Engineering as its official scheduling tool. The front end was built from scratch in Typescript with React and Tailwind CSS, backed by a Spring Boot service deployed on AWS EC2.

projects.name: GodsEye — Video surveillance backend
projects.about: The backend for a surveillance system allowing parents to access live feeds from Raspberry Pi-based cameras in their wards' classrooms. It houses the API endpoints for in-house authentication and OAuth, motion detection, and routines to stream camera frames to authenticated API consumers. It also employs compression of frames for transmission. This project was deployed as a proof of concept for a local edtech initiative seeking to develop a product like Ring.

projects.name: WOPRI
projects.about: A trivia quiz game developed as a Progressive Web Application (PWA). Built with performance and user experience in mind, it was a personal experiment on accessibility and extreme optimization for PWAs. It has a Lighthouse performance rating of 99%.

projects.name: SHANNONIZER
projects.about: In information theory, the entropy of a random variable is the average level of "information", "surprise", or "uncertainty" inherent in the variable's possible outcomes. The concept of information entropy was introduced by Claude Shannon in his 1948 paper "A Mathematical Theory of Communication", and is sometimes called Shannon entropy in his honor. Shannonizer is a Python program for calculating self-information or average information (entropy) of an event or series of events in bits.
